title: Technical Program Manager, EMEA
description:
ABOUT HIYA

At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.

Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.

About the Position

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead delivery of complex carrier and partner integrations enabling Hiya products

This role is delivery-focused, highly cross-functional, and deeply technical. You will be the primary point of contact between Hiya and carriers and partners across EMEA, ensuring each integration is planned, executed, tracked, and delivered. .

You will partner closely with Engineering, Product, Specialists, Customer Success, and external carrier technical teams to bring new product integrations to life.

This role is based in London with an expectation of 3 days/week in-office. Hiya is a global company, with meeting times optimized across timezones.

What You’ll Do

PROGRAM & DELIVERY LEADERSHIP

- Own end-to-end delivery integrations, from kickoff through deployment.

- Define and manage realistic project plans milestones, dependencies, and risk registers.

- Run weekly internal and external technical planning meetings, maintain project tracking docs, and ensure all stakeholders are aligned.

- Ensure carriers and partners deliver their components on time (e.g., solution design inputs, network connectivity, integration configuration, data elements, test dependencies and test results, and delivery artifacts and related sign-offs,).

TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP & PROBLEM SOLVING

- Bring technical fluency in REST APIs, AWS services, and SIP/telephony basics.

- Collaborate with Solution Architect, Engineering and Product to clarify requirements, validate API data and plan delivery.

- Manage completion of Hiya’s technical delivery tasks and delivery lifecycle gates.

- Identify technical blockers early, escalate appropriately, and drive resolution across teams.

STAKEHOLDER & PARTNER MANAGEMENT

- Act as the trusted point of contact for carriers and partners, ensuring expectations, timelines, and responsibilities are clear.
Manage cross-functional communication with Solution Architect, Engineering, Success, Product, and leadership.

- Present clear, concise updates to both technical and non-technical audiences internally and externally.

- Build strong partnerships through collaborative persistence, clarity, and a bias toward action.

PROCESS IMPROVEMENT

- Contribute to improving delivery practices, templates, and tooling for repeatability across future delivery programs.

- Contribute to tailoring delivery framework to align with emerging new product deliveries.

- Identify gaps in process, communication, or documentation and proactively address them.

What You’ll Need to Succeed

- 5+ years in technical program management or complex technical project delivery (SaaS preferred).

- Familiarity with software development lifecycle basics, Jira for ticket management, and program management methodologies is required.

- Experience leading integrations involving APIs, AWS, and complex technical data flows.

- Background in telecom, carriers, SIP/telephony, or adjacent industries

- Proven experience owning large implementations end-to-end, with hands-on involvement in requirements, ris

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Device Platform
description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. 

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. 

About the Role

The Device Platform team owns the backend between Verkada's cloud and the hardware we ship - device provisioning, OTA firmware rollout, and the licensing layer that turns devices into a business. Verkada already operates at millions of devices, and we're scaling the platform for the next order of magnitude - with the consistency, latency, and uptime guarantees our enterprise customers depend on.

Hitting that scale isn't just a technical problem. We're creating the IoT core that every product team across Verkada relies on to accelerate their roadmaps. We do as much cross-team alignment as deep systems design, and hold a high bar on both execution and communication with our peers.

We're five senior engineers today, with a new-grad joining us this summer - and we're hiring more as the platform's reach across Verkada grows. We're high-trust and inclusive: we give and receive feedback directly, we learn out loud, and we get better together because of it.

What You'll Do

• Senior engineers on this team architect, ship, and bring others along. We learn and teach as we build.

• Design and lead major platform features end-to-end, such as the IoT core, the device-metrics platform, or the licensing ledger.

• Lead operational improvements that increase system robustness, reduce pager noise, and help the team learn from incidents when they occur.

• Teach as you ship - through design reviews, code reviews, crisp written communication, and direct mentorship.

• Listen to other Verkada teams, and help drive the platform's roadmap toward the company's biggest long-term bets.

What You Bring

• 6+ years of experience building backend services with consistency, latency, and uptime guarantees at scale.

• Fluency in at least one server language - Python or Go preferred; adjacent languages like Ruby or JavaScript (NodeJs) welcome.

• Skilled at listening to other engineering teams, shaping shared technical direction, and shipping changes they can build on without surprise.

• This role requires U.S. citizenship or permanent residency for FedRAMP compliance, and onsite presence five days per week.

• We want to build an inclusive team. Research consistently shows that candidates from underrepresented groups apply less often than is warranted - if this opportunity is a positive challenge for your career, please apply.

US Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

• Healthcare programs that can be tailored to meet the personal health and financial well-being needs - Premiums are 100% covered for the employee under at least one plan and 80% for family premi

title: Capture Specialist
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Capture Specialist plays a critical role in supporting the organization’s business development and growth objectives by identifying, analyzing, and advancing government and public-sector opportunities from early identification through proposal submission. This role partners closely with business development, technical, and leadership teams to support capture planning, competitive positioning, and proposal alignment.

The Capture Specialist is responsible for monitoring procurement platforms, conducting market and competitive research, supporting stakeholder engagement efforts, and helping shape win strategies that align organizational capabilities with customer needs. The position requires strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills, as well as the ability to manage multiple opportunities simultaneously in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

PRINCIPAL TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

•
Opportunity Identification: Monitor government procurement platforms and industry sources to identify relevant opportunities. Conduct market and competitive research to evaluate feasibility.

•
Strategic Capture Planning: Collaborate with internal teams to develop and execute capture plans that outline win strategies, value propositions, and differentiators.

•
Stakeholder Engagement: Support relationship-building efforts with key decision-makers and stakeholders. Attend industry events, conferences, and networking engagements.

•
Proposal Alignment: Assist in shaping proposal content to reflect the capture strategy and customer expectations. Ensure compliance with RFP/RFQ requirements.

•
Competitive Intelligence: Conduct ongoing analysis of competitors' strengths, weaknesses, and market positioning. Recommend strategy adjustments accordingly.

•
Risk Identification: Assist in identifying potential risks and support the development of mitigation strategies.

•
Leadership Communication: Prepare and present executive summaries, capture updates, and opportunity briefings for senior leadership.

•
Pipeline Management: Maintain accurate records of opportunities in the business development pipeline and federal & local agencies forecasts.

•
General Support: Perform additional tasks as needed to support the business development lifecycle.

• Other Duties

• Performing any other tasks required by the company.

Qualifications

•
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field preferred.

• At least 2 years of experience in business development, capture management, or related roles.

• OR 3+ years of administrative/leadership experience in a professional services environment; 1 year with a bachelor’s degree.

• Understanding of government contracting and procurement processes is highly desirable.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); experience with proposal management tools is a plus.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines.

• Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The position requires normal physical effort when standing, walking, sitting, and/or using office equipment.

title: Brex Rotational Program

description:

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

The Brex Rotational Program

Throughout this 18-20 month program, you'll rotate through two of our G&A teams, learning about areas such as risk management, finance, automation, and data analysis. You'll contribute to critical process improvements and developments, implementing our processes while leveraging AI to streamline workflows and enhance decision-making.

You'll challenge the status quo, bringing insights from each rotation to the next to improve cross-team communication and efficiency. • Strong problem-solving abilities and comfort working through ambiguity.

• Passion for business operations, internal tools, and the application of AI and automation to improve efficiency and enable scale.

• Proven ability to work both independently and in cross-functional teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex ideas clearly and effectively.

• Desire to contribute in a fast-paced environment with a founding team member mindset.

Bonus Points

title: Site Reliability Engineer, Vehicle Software
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Vehicle Software Engineering Teams

Our Vehicle Software Engineering team builds and operates the software that keeps Wayve’s autonomous vehicles running safely in the real world. Within it, the Tools & Infrastructure team owns the reliability stack for vehicle software: observability, incident management, operator tooling, and the automation that lets engineering and operations detect and resolve issues faster. As Wayve scales its autonomous vehicle programs with OEM partners this team is defining what SRE looks like for vehicle-centric systems from the ground up.

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Building and improving tooling, automation, observability, and incident-management processes for vehicle software reliability

- Partnering closely with field engineers, software teams, and operations to diagnose reliability issues and improve system performance

- Owning hands-on debugging across Linux, low-level systems, logs, metrics, traces, and vehicle and production data

- Developing reliability improvements that reduce manual intervention and make issue detection, triage, and recovery faster

- Supporting vehicle-centric operations, including safety-operator tools and the reliability needs of our customer and partner programmes

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

- Reliability for real-world autonomous vehicle operations, not just traditional cloud or platform SRE

- Vehicle safety, operator tooling, observability, and incident management that have a direct impact on production reliability

- Close collaboration with software engineering, operations, and field teams to improve how issues are detected, triaged, and resolved

- Defining the SRE approach for vehicle-centric systems as Wayve scales programmes with partners such as Nissan, Stellantis, Mercedes and Uber.

🙌 You should apply if:

- You write production-quality code every day in Python, C++, or Rust

- You’re comfortable debugging at the Linux and systems level, reading logs, tracing failures, and finding root cause in complex environments

- You have experience with CI/CD, containerisation, networking, distributed systems, databases, and observability/incident-management tooling such as DataDog, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Splunk, Humio or similiar

- You’ve diagnosed complex production or operational systems independently, seeing problems through to resolution rather than just escalating

- You communicate well across engineering, operations, and field teams, and know when to bring others in

- You can be onsite in Sunnyvale at least three days a week to work alongside the field teams you’ll support

- Experience with autonomous vehicles, robotics, embedded systems, large-scale telemetry, or safety-critical environments is a plus, though not required

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. This position in DLB’s Mission Critical Department focuses primarily on hyperscale data centers and related mission critical facilities.
The Power Systems Study Engineer III will have the opportunity to work with and collaborate with all design staff and further develop their power studies expertise. This person will work as part of the Engineering Team to complete short circuit coordination and arc flash studies on a wide variety of mission critical projects.
The Power Systems Study Engineer III will receive limited direction on day-to-day work and general instruction on new projects or assignments.  Will execute and assist project leadership on projects of complex scope.  Will work independently or under limited supervision.
The Power Systems Study Engineer III will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals and values, as well as departmental objectives.
Essential Functions
Guide and Direct Power Systems Studies (80%)
Independently perform Power System Studies for mission critical projects. Activities include but are not limited to the following:

• Equipment Evaluation: Assess the capabilities, ratings, and condition of equipment such as transformers, circuit breakers, and capacitors to determine if they meet system requirements.

• Load Flow Studies: Analyze current and future system load to ensure power delivery without overloading components.

• Short Circuit Analysis: Evaluate potential fault conditions to determine the system's response and ensure that equipment ratings are not exceeded.

• Protection Coordination: Study the settings of protective devices such as relays, circuit breakers, and fuses to ensure they coordinate correctly and provide optimal protection.

• Arc Flash Analysis: Conduct studies to determine potential arc flash hazards, calculate incident energy, and recommend safety practices and protective equipment.

• Transient Stability Analysis: Evaluate the power system's ability to maintain synchronism after large disturbances, such as faults or sudden changes in load, motor starting, etc.

• Prepare incremental and final deliverables including breaker settings tables, TCC’s, arc flash labels, and final reports as required by the project scope.

• Fluent in Power System Study software including one or more of the following:

•

• SKM Powertools

• EasyPower

• ETAP

Project Management & Reporting (20%)

• Assist with proposal development including project scope, schedule and budget

• Timely and effective management of project deliverables including personal workload forecasting and coordination

• Identify potential project scope changes and aid in development of strategies to minimize impact and control deviations from estimated costs and project deadlines

• Perform QAQC peer reviews for projects where he or she is not the lead design engineer / power system study specialist.

• Prepare project reports for internal and external stakeholders for projects which he or she is involved.

Technology, Digital Tools & AI-Enabled Efficiency

• Leverage AI-enabled and digital tools to enhance efficiency, reduce manual effort, and support consistent, high-quality work output.

• Identify opportunities to improve processes and demonstrate a continuous learning mindset, seeking out new technologies, skills, and methods that elevate individual and team

deine position
At 1KOMMA5°, we connect and manage tens of thousands of distributed energy devices at scale. As a (Senior) IoT Cloud Engineer, you will own the cloud side of our IoT Platform that ingests, routes, and observes every message flowing between our gateway fleet and our cloud services.

• Take ownership of our systems at the intersection of Cloud Services and residential IoT Gateways

• Operate and evolve our Kubernetes-based IoT Cloud Platform, including the deployment, scaling, and hardening of our connectivity and fleet services

• Develop and run our Eclipse Hono stack as the messaging backbone between gateways and the cloud

• Design, build and operate features around fleet management enabling the lifecycle of gateways from production line to field

• Integrate tightly with Mender to operate safe OTA rollouts across the fleet.

• Contribute to load and resilience tests to prove the platform scales and to find limits before our customers do

• Build and own the observability pipelines for the IoT Platform and turn metrics into automated monitors, alerts, and self-healing mechanisms

• Build data pipelines and BI models to turn raw data into fleet insights

• Work collaboratively with product managers, data engineers, IoT engineers, as well as cloud engineers to understand problems, support discoveries, and create solutions enabling a scalable virtual power plant

• Foster a culture of experiment-driven innovation within the team

• Cloud & Infra: Google Cloud Platform, GKE (Kubernetes), Cloud Run, Terraform/IaC

• Messaging & IoT: Eclipse Hono, MQTT, Mender

• Data & BI: PostgreSQL, BigQuery, SQLMesh, Looker

• Observability: Datadog, OpenTelemetry

• Languages: TypeScript (Nest.js), Java, Go

• DevOps: CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions)

dein profil

title: Engineer II/ Senior Engineer, Robotics Platform Evaluation
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila is building a dedicated platform evaluation function within our robotics organization. The team tests and benchmarks alternative robotics platforms, including mobile manipulators, AMRs and AGVs, and other form factors, against our current production baseline. Consistent methodology across platforms is the point: results have to be directly comparable to be useful.

As a Robotics Platform Evaluation Engineer, you own robots end to end. You unbox and commission new hardware, integrate it with our software stack and infrastructure, execute the full test program, and turn the results into decision-ready comparisons that inform which platforms we adopt.

This is a hands-on, systems-level role. You will be in the lab working directly with hardware, not reviewing spec sheets. You will also shape the evaluation methodology and the tooling behind it, so each platform assessment runs faster and more consistently than the last.

What You'll Be Building

• Commission new robotics platforms from unboxing through integration with our stack

• Own end-to-end evaluation of assigned platforms, from test plan to benchmark report

• Run test suites spanning navigation, manipulation, perception, and controls

• Integrate platforms with ROS2 and Nav2, adapting drivers, configurations, and interfaces

• Characterize manipulator, gripper, and AMR/AGV performance against comparable baselines

• Extend the shared evaluation framework and tooling for future platform assessments

• Flag integration issues, safety concerns, and platform limitations early and clearly

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Professional experience deploying robotics platforms in production, commercial, or applied R&D settings

• Hands-on ROS2 and Nav2 experience in real deployments, not simulation alone

• Experience with manipulation and pick-and-place, including motion planning and grasp execution

• Experience with controls for robot arms or mobile bases

• Experience integrating and calibrating camera or lidar perception pipelines

• Direct experience with AMRs/AGVs or 6 to 7 DoF arms, including grippers and end effectors

• Track record turning test results into clear, decision-ready comparisons

Bonus Points For

• Evaluated or compared multiple robotics platforms or vendors head to head

• Experience with mobile manipulators, meaning an arm mounted on a mobile base

• Experience with robotics simulation tools (Isaac Sim, Gazebo, or similar) for platform validation

• Built internal tooling or frameworks for standardized robot testing

• Background in industrial, warehouse, logistics, or manufacturing automation

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset-AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.

THE ROLE

As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

- Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

- Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

- Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

- Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.  Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics,

title: Associate Systems Support Engineer
description:
Job Summary
We are seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented Associate Systems Support Engineer to join our IT operations team. The successful candidate will be responsible for monitoring and maintaining the performance of critical systems, ensuring the uptime and availability of applications and infrastructure. • Participate in root cause analysis (RCA) for incidents to prevent future occurrences and improve system reliability.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

• Familiarity with application performance monitoring tools such as AppDynamics, LogicMonitor, and Azure Monitor.

• Basic knowledge of SQL databases, including monitoring and troubleshooting techniques.

• Understanding of Windows Server administration and IIS management.

• Experience with monitoring server uptime, performance metrics, and alert management.

• Proficient in troubleshooting system issues and performing root cause analysis.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail to ensure high-quality service delivery.

title: Staff / Principal Security Engineer, AI Safety and Security
locationText: Cambridge, MA USA; London, UK; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila is developing AI systems for scientific discovery, connecting advanced models with scientific tools and automated laboratories. As these systems become more capable, we need to understand how they could be misused or compromised, which protections matter most, and how to establish that those protections work together.

We're hiring an experienced security practitioner to lead this work at the boundary between AI safety and security. You will investigate real systems, develop threat models, test important assumptions and recommend the protections needed for particular capabilities and deployments. Your work will address both dangerous misuse and the protection of sensitive models, data and research.

This is an opportunity to help shape a developing area of AI safety through security practice. You will combine technical investigation with careful analysis and clear writing, working closely with our established Security team, researchers and engineers to turn findings into implemented improvements.

You will bring security depth and develop your understanding of model capabilities, evaluations and safeguards through that work. Prior experience in AI safety is welcome, but not required.

What You'll Be Building

• Threat-model consequential systems and capabilities. Investigate how dangerous misuse or compromise could occur across models, deployed services and scientific workflows. Identify the relevant actors, access routes and failure paths, and the protections that could interrupt them.

• Test the assumptions behind our defenses. Examine architectures, code, configurations and operational evidence. Run focused adversarial tests, build prototypes and investigate weaknesses, including situations where several protections depend on the same underlying system.

• Shape the protections needed for safe deployment. Turn dangerous-capability assessments into concrete security requirements. Assess how compromise of models, sensitive assets or supporting systems changes the safety assessment, drawing on personnel, physical and other security specialists where relevant.

• Make evidence-based recommendations. Define what evidence would demonstrate that important controls and safeguards work together. Combine findings from model evaluations and security testing, explain the remaining uncertainty, and recommend improvements or conditions for use.

• Carry findings through to practical improvements. Work with Security, Safety and engineering owners to prioritize changes, specify acceptance criteria and verify the results. Make clear recommendations about which gaps require attention first and why.

• Anticipate what more capable systems will require. Identify where changes in capability, access or deployment call for stronger protections. Help teams plan security work with long lead times, and update assessments as systems change or new evidence emerges.

• Develop methods that others can use. Turn your investigations into clear threat models, assessment methods and technical guidance. Help Safety and Security colleagues apply the approach to new problems and build a shared understanding of the evidence behind decisions.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Substantial hands-on security experience and deep expertise in at least one relevant discipline , such as security architecture, application or infrastructure security, offensive security, or incident response. You can reason across disciplines and identify when specialist judgment is needed.

• A record of resolving consequential security problems. You have investigated ambiguous risks, challenged designs and followed improvements through to validation, including work involving several teams.

• Strong technical judgment. You can examine unfamiliar systems, scrutinize code and configurations where relevant, and use technical investigation or testing to distinguish plausible claims from demonstrated protection.

High expectations. Real ownership. Things change fast and we don't apologize for it. You'll work with smart people who push you, a product that keeps getting better, and a team that's genuinely building something new.
We'll probably give you more to own than you expected. That's on purpose.

Act as an entrepreneur : prendre ses responsabilités, jouer collectif, oser essayer et accepter l’échec.
Innovate or die : remettre en question le statu quo, aussi impossible que cela puisse paraître.
Faster is better : privilégier la rapidité à la perfection, et l’alignement au débat.
No limit : viser la lune tout en restant humble.

title: Principal Data Engineer, Data Quality & Datasets Pipelines
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Datasets Team

Wayve’s Datasets team own the driving data that our AI Driver learns from, covering ingestion, annotation (automatic and manual), retrieval and data quality. Our data is growing from hundreds of petabytes towards exabyte scale, and not all of it is equally valuable for training. This team decides what we keep and where, and builds the systems that make those decisions work in practice.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Implement and iterate filtering, retention and offload policies across hot, cold, archive and delete storage

- Build the data movement and pipelines that our pre-ingestion selection model depends on

- Decide where and how selection models run, balancing compute cost against data value

- Build early, low-compute decision points that avoid expensive standardisation and enrichment of low-value data

- Work with the storage and data infra teams, and monitor data quality to make sure our datasets reflect what model training needs

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

- Turning our dataset strategy into working systems: moving, filtering, retaining and offloading driving data at hundreds of petabytes

- The engineering behind our pre-ingestion selection mode(s)l: how data moves, where the model runs and how offload policies work

- Delivering large, measurable storage-cost savings through early, low-compute decisions

- Making sure our datasets contain the most useful behavioural and environmental coverage for training. This is as much a data quality challenge as a software engineering one

- Working as a pair with our dataset strategy lead (who design and builds the models) and closely with the data infra team, shipping practical solutions quickly

 

👤 You should apply if:

- You’re a senior data or software engineer who has run data ingestion or data quality pipelines at petabyte scale

- You’re strong in Python and Spark, with cloud data engineering experience

- You have good judgement on data filtering and quality, and know how to check you haven’t discarded valuable data

- You ship practical solutions quickly and are comfortable iterating on live systems

- You’re a software engineer at heart, building the systems around models rather than the models themselves

- You enjoy working closely with data infra and storage teams

- You bring experience in AV, robotics, fleet data or high-volume IoT, or with retention, offload and data lifecycle policies (a bonus rather than a requirement)

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core A

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier-from solo founders to established enterprises-united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

Your role

Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We’re at the center of this, and we think the best work is still in front of us.

• Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting).

We free clinicians and operations from manual work a machine can do reliably and safely, in a domain where mistakes have real clinical and compliance consequences.
It's a full-stack product team, not an AI lab: we ship UI, backend workflows, integrations, and AI features side by side, and we measure them the same way.
The team works closely with Product, Engineering, MedOps, Clinical people. We're hiring an Product Analyst to own analytics for the team end-to-end as our automated surface area grows.
The role
You'll be the Product Analyst for the team - across everything we ship, both classical product features and AI-powered ones. You'll turn the production behavior of our systems into evidence the team can act on: which parts work, where they fail silently, and what to fix next. The work blends product analytics, AI evaluation, and operational analysis.
Responsibilities

• Own the full product analytics stack for features the team ships - discovery and sizing, experiment design and analysis, funnel and adoption analysis, post-release impact assessment - across both AI-powered and conventional product features.

• Analyze production behavior of AI and automation workflows across clinical and operational journeys.

• Investigate hallucinations, silent failures, and quality degradation in AI-generated output.

• Work directly with logs, transcripts, generated artifacts, and operational data to find patterns dashboards miss.

• Design evaluations for AI quality - both automated and human review - and close the loop into prompt and product changes.

• Build monitoring and dashboards for AI and automation health, and the operational metrics they roll up to.

• Measure business and operational impact of automation initiatives and surface the risks they introduce.

• Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Clinical, MedOps, and Legal to support fast decisions under ambiguity.

Requirements

• 3+ years of experience in Product Analytics/Operational Analytics/Data Analytics, or analytics roles within complex production systems.

• Understanding of AI, ML, and LLM systems.

• Hands-on experience evaluating LLM or AI output - prompt iteration, eval frameworks and human review pipelines is a strong plus.

• Effective, structured written and verbal communication - able to turn analysis into crisp, decision-ready writeups that non-analysts can act on.

• Comfort in ambiguous, fast-changing environments where ground truth often has to be constructed.

• Strong product / operational analytics background, comfortable owning metrics end-to-end and writing SQL and Python code against messy production data.

• Fluent Russian; English level B2 or higher,

• Ability to work CET-overlapping hours in a B2B format.

Nice to Have

• Experience evaluating LLM outputs or AI systems.

• Previous experience in Data Science or Machine Learning.

What we offer

• Opportunity to work on products at the intersection of Product Analytics and AI.

• Real influence on product direction and engineering practices

• High-impact work in a product-driven medical tech company

• Startup environment: fast iteration, high ownership, minimal bureaucracy

You'll also be involved in the management and oversight of our insurance partners and outsourced service providers, helping make sure the right operating rhythms are in place and contractual and regulatory requirements are met.

- Lead insurer-focused projects and regulatory workstreams, such as onboarding new insurance partners, operational resilience and GFSC deliverables.

- Support ZIL's internal audit programme, coordinating reviews, working with the business on findings and making sure actions are closed out.

- Further enhance ZIL's governance, strengthening our frameworks and controls, proactively documenting procedures and keeping policies up to date, clearly owned and on their review cycle.

- Support the oversight of our outsourced service providers, including Zego MGA. Job Title: CNC Machinist

 

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"-we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge-on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

 

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month-not next year-this is your playground.

 

Position Summary

You are the second half of a two-person machine shop, working alongside our Machine Shop Manager to keep the spindles turning across a wider band of hours than one person can. You bring about five years of stick time on CNC mills and lathes, you program your own parts in Mastercam, and you handle the rest of a working shop: manual machines, sawing, deburring, tapping, fitting and inspection. The shop builds the hardware EDDA's R&D and test program runs on - turret structure, mounts, drive parts, fixtures and test rigs - often from a CAD model that landed that morning.

 
 

Essential Duties

- Program your own parts: CAD to toolpaths in Mastercam, tooling, speeds and feeds, prove-out at the machine, G-code edits at the control.

- Set up and run CNC mills and lathes: workholding, offsets, probing, first article to print, then hold tolerance across the run.

- Do the rest of the shop's work: manual mill and lathe, saw, drill press, tapping, deburring, press fits and inserts, light fitting and assembly.

- Inspect and document: hand tools on a surface plate, GD&T, first-article records - in aluminum, steel, stainless, plastics and the occasional titanium.

Requirements

- Experience: about 5 years (3-7) in a working machine shop, with real stick time on both CNC mills and CNC lathes.

- CNC programming (required): you write your own programs from CAD in CAM - we run Mastercam - read and edit G-code at the control, and have proven out your own programs. Running someone else's program does not meet this bar.

- Setup and operation: workholding, fixturing, tool and work offsets, first-article proof-out; you hold ±0.001" when the print calls for it.

- General shop process and inspection: manual machining, sawing, drilling, tapping, deburring and fitting; read GD&T and inspect with calipers, micrometers, height and bore gauges.

- Flexible schedule: willing to work a staggered shift coordinated with the Machine Shop Manager - early starts some weeks, late finishes others.

- Compliance and physical: U.S. citizenship, ability to pass a background check, lift 50 lb and stand for long periods.

 

Nice‑to‑Have

- Prototype or R&D shop background: one-offs, fast turnaround, incomplete drawings, engineers at your elbow.

- 4th/5-axis milling, live-tooling lathes, Fanuc macros and probing cycles.

- CAD, not just CAM: model a fixture or simple part in SolidWorks and design your own workholding.

- Secondary processes: TIG welding, sheet metal, 3-D printing, or spec'ing anodize, plating and heat treat.

- Weapon, firearms, aerospace or defense hardware; security clearance or the ability to obtain one.

 

Benefits

title: Customer Success Strategy & Operations Manager
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

CUSTOMER SUCCESS STRATEGY & OPERATIONS MANAGER

Revenue Operations · Full-time · San Francisco, New York or Austin

We’re hiring a Customer Success Strategy & Operations Manager to help us deliver customer value and reach. We built our foundation around our coding product and engineering users. As we expand into general knowledge work and new use cases, our customer value delivery needs to evolve with it.

Our customers vary in type and size, and our goal is to unlock exceptional value for everyone. You’ll begin as a generalist across Customer Success, with a focus on solutions architecture, digital and scaled motions and the opportunity to develop deep expertise in a business unit end to end as we grow. You’ll partner with senior leaders to understand what’s working, what isn’t, and how to adapt the customer experience to drive value realization, retention, and growth.

You bring an analytical mindset and an orientation toward rapid experimentation. You’ll identify usage patterns that predict customer growth or churn, turn them into signals and plays the team can use, and help run experiments to learn what works so we can apply those learnings forward. The teams you will support are technical and experienced. They need a strategy and operations partner who brings insight and rigor that helps them make the right big bets and move with pace in bringing them to life.

You’ll be a thought partner to senior leadership and a hands-on operator who builds the models, insights and systems that help our teams stay agile and deliver on our goals. This isn’t a pure strategy role or a pure analyst role: you’ll set direction with leadership in one meeting and build the model behind it in the next.

Our organization is flat, and our team is small and talent-dense. You’ll have an outsized impact on our customers and the company’s trajectory. We’re looking for someone who is truth-seeking, collaborative, analytical, and loves to build.

What you’ll do

- Design segmentation and coverage models so each customer gets the service model that drives growth

- Build headcount and capacity models so we invest in the right places at the right time

- Guide and define the metrics that matter for the CS org, and the compensation models that reward the right outcomes

- Track business performance, find what’s driving the trends, and turn it into specific actions and strategies with owners

- Build the leadership operating cadence (business reviews, planning, decision forums) so decisions get made quickly with good data

- Build repeatable metrics, dashboards and applications that put the right KPIs in front of the right people to drive decisions and actions, from frontline teams to leadership

- Analyze product usage to find the patterns that predict activation, expansion, retention and churn

- Help design and run rapid experiments with clear hypotheses and control groups, then scale what works and retire what doesn’t

- Help build the scaled engagement model as a system: how data, tooling, digital touchpoints and human coverage fit together

You may be a fit if

- You have experience in revenue strategy & operations, customer strategy & operations or business op
